To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TSC that are based on the quinoline and di-2-piridine scaffolds exhibit a promising anticancer activity against a panel of human cancer cell lines.
the tested compounds exhibit a potent cytotoxic activity against the tested panel of cancer cell types, including colon and breast cancer cells and glioblastoma cells.

1) the tested TSC are able to chelate both iron and copper; 2) they induce cell cycle arrest at the G0/G1 phase and apoptosis via a p53-independent pathway; 3) they induce a decrease in the intracellular glutathione level; and 4) the tested compounds exhibit a high selectivity against the cancer cell lines that are characterized by a low level of iron regulatory protein-1 (IRP1).

the TSC that are based on quinoline and di-2-pyrindione scaffolds are the most promising candidates for further development.

the TSC are a promising class of anticancer agents.
